title: Red Sox, Orioles are both winners in bold Adley Rutschman deal: MLB trade grades
content:
The Athletic has live coverage of the 2026 MLB Trade Deadline.

Orioles get: C Carlos Narváez, RHP Anthony Eyanson, RHP Kyson Witherspoon, OF Enddy Azocar, PTBNL

Red Sox get: C Adley Rutschman, C Jake Rogers

Orioles: A
Red Sox: A

First, the easy part: this is a massive haul for the Orioles. Eyanson made Keith Law’s updated top 50, Witherspoon was a 2025 first-rounder, and Azocar is a teenager having a breakout season.  It’s the kind of package that will make every Red Sox fan squirm.

But it’s also the kind of trade-deadline deal the Red Sox haven’t made in more than a decade. Even when they’ve been in the playoff hunt, the Red Sox have lately settled for role players and rentals, which worked to supplement a loaded roster in 2018 but hasn’t worked since — and this year’s team needed far more than a platoon hitter or middle-inning reliever.

The Red Sox took a massive swing by trading for a player who was supposed to be the cornerstone of a division rival and will instead fill a position where the Red Sox haven’t had an All-Star since Jason Varitek retired in 2011 (we’re not counting A.J. Pierzynski, who was well past his All-Star years when he arrived for a partial season in 2014). Rutschman has been an All-Star in three of five big league seasons, including this one, and despite missing time with several short-term injuries, he has again been one of the most valuable catchers in the sport this year. He has bounced back from a disappointing 2025 to post above-average offensive numbers to go with his usual strong defensive metrics. That’s a substantial upgrade over Narváez and Connor Wong, who have combined to perform at or below replacement level this season.

There’s a lot of long-term risk here because of the star potential heading to Baltimore, and this could be a Red Sox F in the long-term analysis. But this is what an all-in move looks like, and the Red Sox finally made one. — Chad Jennings

Orioles: A-
Red Sox: B+

It’s the right move for both teams, given where they are and what they need. The Red Sox need to build on their momentum and play into October. The Orioles need pitching depth if they’re ever going to win consistently. This deal helps advance both goals, with a slight edge to the Orioles because of Rutschman’s limited club control (he’s eligible for free agency after 2027).

Rutschman was the No. 1 pick in the 2019 MLB Draft, the backbone of the Orioles’ plan, under then-new GM Mike Elias, to stockpile top-of-the-draft prospects in hopes of a sustained run of success. But after a surprise division title in 2023 and a wild-card berth in 2024, the Orioles have fallen back to the pack.

Trading Rutschman represents a significant shift for an organization that has been hesitant to break up its young core. It signals that Elias and the owner, David Rubenstein, believe that business as usual will not get the Orioles back to the World Series for the first time since 1983.

Rutschman made the All-Star team in 2023 and 2024, but he has gone backward over the past two years, even though he was an All-Star again in 2026. Starting with the second half of the 2024 season, Rutschman has hit just .227 with 20 home runs in 777 at-bats.

Even so, he’s a 28-year-old switch hitter with a respectable .251/.331/.433 slash line this season. Rutschman is a major upgrade behind the plate for the Red Sox, whose catchers have hit a meager .219/.305/.310 this season.

The trade confirms the Orioles’ commitment to Samuel Basallo as their catcher of the future. Basallo, who turns 22 next week, is signed to an eight-year, $67 million contract with a club option for 2034, the kind of bargain contract that probably made a Rutschman trade inevitable. (Basallo has shoulder inflammation now, so Narvaez presumably takes over catching duties for the moment.)

Given Rutschman’s pending free agency after 2027, it’s a relatively short-term play for Boston. But with 23 wins in their past 26 games — and just two playoff appearances in the past seven seasons — the Red Sox are finally focused on the present.

In return, the Orioles got Boston’s first- and third-round draft picks from 2025: Witherspoon and Eyanson, a pair of 21-year-old right-handed starters. Eyanson, who pitched at LSU and appeared in the Futures Game last month, has been especially dominant this season.

Azocar, 19, is a center fielder who is (obviously) further away from the majors. Azocar has shown power this season at two Class-A levels, with 18 home runs and a .540 slugging percentage. — Tyler Kepner
